# Scope §verify_before_assert by claim class: code and runtime claims are re-run, record claims with receipts are cited, business text gets one fact check at the final version

## Why this exists

**The operator, Mon Nov 2 20:5x CET, to the team:** redundant verify-before-assert on business items that already carry their verification is a failure pattern for the whole team, not one seat's method — "vba matters a lot when writing code or architectures; for business items too much VBA on items that already got that will fill up context windows fast for redundant work, then hitting compaction and starting over at zero."

§verify_before_assert (`.claude/CLAUDE.md`, AGENTS.md) is written without a claim class: *"Before asserting any factual claim … run the empirical tool that would falsify it."* Read literally, a number that already sits in the record beside its query gets re-run by every seat that touches it.

## The specimen (Nov 2, the YC application)

- The same submission-day counts were measured by three seats within one hour (Grace 15:28Z, Mnemosyne 15:40Z and 15:49–15:52Z, Clio until the search API cut her off at 16:10Z); two of the three new receipts then needed a second run anyway because the first seat's labels were inferred (business #27, Grace's second run 16:12Z).
- The author seat's context window went from 12 % to 48 % of 1M across the lane (measured by the app's usage card at 15:24Z and 16:39Z); most of it was measurement, rewrites that measurement steered, and the peer corrections of both.
- The measuring steered the text: measurable facts (a roster, merge identities, PR counts) were promoted into the pitch over the true thesis, and were withdrawn (business #30, review 5741744044 and its withdrawal).
- The record's authors had already verified the claims where they live (`strategy/areas/inventory-moat.md`, the Nov 1 funding notes, `decisions-in-force.md`), with their anchors.

## The tension to resolve, not paper over

neo #15780 holds the opposite rule for runtime state: *"having checked is not a durable property … re-run rather than reuse."* Both are right for their class. The rule needs the class.

## Proposed amendment (§verify_before_assert, one paragraph)

> **Scope by claim class.** (1) **Code, runtime and architecture claims** — re-run the falsifying tool every time; a check is spent the turn it ran (#15780). (2) **Record claims that already carry a receipt** (a number beside its query, a decision beside its anchor, a date beside its commit) — cite the anchor; re-measure only when the claim is being *changed* or the anchor is missing. (3) **Business and pitch text** — mine the record first (nothing to re-invent), write from the anchors, and run **one consolidated fact check at the final version**, never a per-point sweep per revision. Re-measuring a receipt to add a number to a pitch is the anti-pattern: it costs the window, invites compaction, and steers the text toward what is measurable instead of what is true.

## Acceptance

- [ ] AC-1 §verify_before_assert in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and AGENTS.md carries the claim-class scope above (bytes added ≤ bytes of the prior-art citation it replaces, per `turn-memory-pre-flight`), with #15780 cited for class (1) and this ticket for classes (2)–(3)
- [ ] AC-2 `.agents/skills/blog-post` (which already carries "why would the audience NOT click?") and the funding/pitch workflow name the single final-version fact check as the gate, not per-revision V-B-A
- [ ] AC-3 the specimen above is the retrieval anchor in the amended paragraph's commit message, not in the rule text

## Out of scope

Any change to class (1); the Fleet Manager; automation of fact checks.

## Related

#10469 (V-B-A's origin), #15780 (freshness for runtime checks); business #26, #27, #30 (the specimen; private); `turn-memory-pre-flight`.

handoff: self-select — a seat with window; the author's seat is at 82 % of its weekly allowance.
